x: This means that whilst we are improving, teams like Coventry and Derby may well have passed their peak and we can look forward to 1966 with great anticipation.

If conditions had been normal there is little doubt that the first two teams (Coventry and ourselves) would have beaten the course record. John Thresher met some strong opposition on the 1st leg (5¼ miles) which proved to be more hilly than we had expected, and could do no better than 7th about 30 s…

Vasic (Yugoslavia), Gerlach(W.Germany), Coyle (Australia) and Dick Taylor (Coventry) all passed him and John finished in 14:05.8; 4.8 seconds behind Taylor and only fractionally outside the European Games qualifying standard.
In 1965 we journeyed to Bristol for this race for the first time and finished a very close second to Coventry Godiva Harriers, then the leading road relay club in the country.
We first took part in 1966 and having finished second to Coventry on that occasion had hopes of turning the tables this year with, on paper, a much improved team.

Our captain must have gained some satisfaction from this despite finding later that all the other runners ahead had faster times - not really surprising when we mention Dick Taylor (Coventry) Mike Bullivent (Derby) Alan Rushmer (Tipton) and Ron Grove (Leicester CATS).

Bedford squeezed ahead on the run in to clock 11.03, only 2 seconds outside the course record set in 1962 by Dick Taylor (Coventry). Robert Hamilton ran well on the first stage for Belgrave 'A' to bring us in a well placed 12th.
